mainTopic: When one unfit witness ruins a whole group's testimony, and who counts as a witness at all
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a group of witnesses where one turns out to be a relative or otherwise unfit. רבי יוסי says the whole group falls only in דיני נפשות. רבי says it falls in דיני ממונות too. The משנה adds that the group is ruined only by people who came as witnesses and gave התראה, not by bystanders like two brothers in a crowd. In the גמרא, רבא says many witnesses join into one testimony only within תוך כדי דיבור, and רבינא explains that each witness must begin right after the one before him. רב פפא then challenges רבי עקיבא's rule: the victim, and even the killer himself, saw the act, so shouldn't they ruin the testimony? רבא answers from the פסוק 'יקום דבר' that only people who come to establish the matter in court count as witnesses. רבא then explains that the court asks people whether they came to watch or to testify. The amud ends with an argument about the final הלכה: שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, and רב נחמן rules like רבי.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits the rule to capital cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that one unfit witness ruins the whole group only in דיני נפשות. In דיני ממונות the testimony stands with the remaining kosher witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: When does this rule apply? In capital cases. But in money cases, the testimony stands with the remaining witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יוסי, who puts a limit on the rule that one unfit witness cancels the whole group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just taught that if one witness in a group is a relative or unfit, all of them are thrown out. רבי יוסי says this strict result belongs only to דיני נפשות, where the court is extra careful. In דיני ממונות, we simply ignore the unfit witness and judge by the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (a phrase that introduces a limit on a rule)
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
Monetary cases
The testimony stands with the rest of the witnesses

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: He means the rule just taught: one relative or unfit witness cancels the whole group.

phrases.english: In capital cases.
But in monetary cases,
the testimony will stand with the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rule (from the previous section) that one unfit witness cancels the whole group, and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One unfit witness cancels the group only in דיני נפשות. In דיני ממונות the remaining witnesses' testimony stands.

steps.title: רבי says the rule applies to money cases too
steps.stepSummary: רבי disagrees with רבי יוסי and says that one unfit witness ruins the whole group in both דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: It is the same in money cases and in capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) argues with רבי יוסי and says there is no difference between the two kinds of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the group of witnesses is one single testimony, whatever kind of case it is. So if one part is unfit, all of it falls, even in a money case.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; the same rule for both

steps.confusionAlert: When the משנה says just "רבי" with no other name, it means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה. It is not a general word for "a rabbi."

phrases.english: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: It is the same for monetary cases and for capital cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוסי's limit and gives the opposite view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One unfit witness cancels the whole group in both monetary and capital cases.

steps.title: The rule applies only when they came as witnesses and warned him
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the rule: the whole group falls only when the witnesses gave התראה (a warning) to the sinner. People who just happened to see, like two brothers among the crowd, do not ruin everyone else's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when does this apply? When they warned them. But when they did not warn them, what are two brothers supposed to do if they saw someone kill a person?!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a big limit: an unfit person cancels the group only if he acted as a witness by warning the sinner. Someone who just happened to be there does not ruin anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving התראה shows that a person stepped forward to be a witness, so he becomes part of the group's testimony. A bystander never joined the group, so his being unfit does not touch it. Otherwise a killer could go free just because two brothers happened to be standing in the crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: And when? (introduces a limit on when the rule applies)
They warned. From הַתְרָאָה, the warning given to a sinner before he acts
Two brothers (they are relatives, so they cannot testify together)
Killed a person

steps.whatToRemember: An unfit person cancels the group only if he joined it as a witness by giving התראה. Bystanders who just saw what happened do not ruin the testimony of the kosher witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the strict rule does not let sinners escape just because unfit people happened to be nearby.

phrases.english: And when does this apply?
When they warned them.
phrases.notes: The witnesses warned the sinners. That warning shows they came forward as witnesses.

phrases.english: But when they did not warn them,
what should two brothers do
who saw someone who killed a person?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit on when the cancel-the-group rule applies at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unfit person cancels the group only when the witnesses gave התראה. Accidental onlookers do not.

steps.title: רבא: all witnesses must testify within a short time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבא, who adds a condition to the earlier משנה's rule that a hundred witnesses count like two. They count as one testimony only if they all testified בתוך כדי דיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. רבא said: And that is only when they all testified within the time of a short phrase of speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבא adds a condition: many witnesses count as one joined testimony only if they all testify close together in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה taught that a hundred witnesses are treated like two. That is why one unfit witness can cancel all of them. רבא says this joining happens only when the witnesses testify בתוך כדי דיבור. If there is a longer gap, they are not one testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
And that is only when... (adds a condition)
Within the time it takes to say a short phrase

phrases.english: Gemara
Rava said:
And that is only when they all testified
phrases.notes: "That" points back to the משנה's rule that a hundred witnesses are like two.

phrases.english: within the time of a short phrase of speech.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְהוּא שֶׁהֵעִידוּ כּוּלָּם בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a condition on the משנה's rule that many witnesses count as one testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Many witnesses join into one testimony only if they testify within תוך כדי דיבור.

steps.title: A hundred witnesses can't fit in such a short time
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי challenges רבא: תוך כדי דיבור is only as long as a student's greeting to his rebbe. A hundred witnesses will always take much longer than that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: Now, how long is "within the time of speech"? As long as a student's greeting to his teacher. A hundred witnesses take much more than that!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי attacks רבא's condition and says that, read simply, it can never be met.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תוך כדי דיבור is only a few seconds, the time it takes to say "שלום עליך רבי." If all hundred testimonies had to fit into that, it could never happen. Then the משנה's case of a hundred witnesses would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, after all (opens a reasoning that leads to a challenge)
What is it like? What are the details?
A student's greeting to his teacher
They are much more

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי תּוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר הֵיכִי דָּמֵי –
phrases.english: Now, how long is "within the time of speech"?
As long as a student's greeting to his teacher.
phrases.notes: That greeting is "שלום עליך רבי". It takes just a few seconds.

phrases.english: A hundred witnesses take much more than that!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: מִכְּדִי תּוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that all the witnesses must testify within תוך כדי דיבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תוך כדי דיבור is only a few seconds long. A hundred testimonies can never fit into it, so the condition would make the משנה's case impossible.

steps.title: Each witness only needs to follow right after the one before
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that רבא meant each witness must begin within תוך כדי דיבור of the previous witness. All hundred do not have to fit inside one short time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Each and every one testifies within the time of speech of his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by explaining what רבא really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The short time limit is not for the whole group. It is the gap allowed between one witness finishing and the next one starting. As long as there is no long break anywhere, the testimonies form one unbroken chain, and they count as a single testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Each and every one
His fellow; here, the witness right before him

steps.whatToRemember: Many witnesses join into one testimony when each one starts within תוך כדי דיבור of the one before him, with no long breaks in the chain.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבינא is answering רב אחא מדפתי.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל חַד וְחַד בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: Each and every one testifies within the time of speech of his fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כׇּל חַד וְחַד בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 and saves רבא's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All hundred testimonies must fit inside one short span of time.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each witness must begin within תוך כדי דיבור of the witness before him, which makes one unbroken chain.

steps.title: Quoting רבי עקיבא's rule about the third witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא from the משנה. The third witness in the פסוק is mentioned to make things stricter, so a large group is treated just like two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: The third witness was not mentioned [to be lenient], etc. And just as with two witnesses, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a short line from the משנה with רבי עקיבא's opinion. It is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that one unfit witness ruins the whole group, the same way one unfit witness ruins a pair. The 'כו׳' means the rest of the משנה is assumed. רב פפא is about to test how far this rule goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The third witness mentioned in the פסוק ('two witnesses or three witnesses')
Short for 'etc.' The rest of the quoted text is assumed
'Just as two': a group is compared to a pair of witnesses

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says
The third did not come, etc.
phrases.notes: The third witness wasn't written in the פסוק to go easy on him but to be strict, so he's treated like the other two.

phrases.english: And just as two, etc.
phrases.notes: Just as one bad witness out of two ruins the pair, one bad witness ruins a big group.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לֹא בָּא שְׁלִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to an earlier line of the משנה to analyze it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group of witnesses is like a pair: if one is unfit, the whole testimony falls.

steps.title: Should the murdered victim ruin the testimony?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if anyone unfit who saw the act ruins the group, the victim saw his own murder. So he should ruin the testimony and save the killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But if so, the murdered person should save [the killer]!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבי עקיבא's rule. He shows that the rule seems to lead to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The victim saw the murder, but he cannot testify about his own case, so he counts as an unfit witness. If one unfit witness ruins everyone, then no murderer could ever be punished.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if so': takes a rule to its extreme to show a problem
The murdered person, the victim
'Should save' the accused from punishment

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But if that is so,
the murdered one should save [the killer]!
phrases.notes: The victim saw it happen but can't be a witness in his own case, so he'd be the 'bad witness' that ruins the group.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rule that one unfit witness ruins the whole group
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The victim is an unfit eyewitness to every murder, so every murder testimony should fall.

steps.title: The killer is punished when he struck from behind
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we only punish the killer in a case where he killed the victim from behind, so the victim never saw it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he killed him from behind.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by limiting the case. The victim didn't see anything, so he isn't a witness at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the victim never saw the act, he can't be counted among the witnesses. Then there is no unfit witness to ruin the group.

keyTerms.meaning: From behind him, so the victim didn't see
'When' or 'in a case where': limits the case
He killed him

phrases.english: When he killed him from behind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the victim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The victim always sees the murder and ruins the testimony
steps.terutzMaskana: The killer is punished in a case where the victim did not see the act

steps.title: Should the victim of רביעה ruin the testimony?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא pushes again: in the sin of lying with a male, the victim surely knows what happened. So he should ruin the testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who was sodomized should save [the sinner]!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a second case where the victim seems to always be an eyewitness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A murder can happen without the victim seeing it. But in this sin the victim is directly involved, so it seems he must be an unfit eyewitness who ruins the group.

keyTerms.meaning: The one acted upon in the forbidden act of lying with a male
The forbidden act of lying with a male (or an animal)

phrases.english: The one who was sodomized should save [him]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the challenge to a new case after the first answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the victim did not see
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this sin the victim is involved in the act, so he seems to always be an eyewitness.

steps.title: This sinner too is punished when it was from behind
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: we punish him only when he did it from behind, so the victim did not see it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he did it to him from behind.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer uses the same idea again. The victim didn't see, so he isn't a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being involved in the act is not the same as seeing it. Only someone who actually saw can count as a witness who ruins the group.

keyTerms.meaning: When he did the forbidden act to him

phrases.english: When he did it to him from behind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second challenge the same way as the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The victim always sees the act
steps.terutzMaskana: The punishment applies in a case where the victim did not see

steps.title: Should the sinner himself ruin the testimony?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's strongest question: the killer always sees what he does himself. So he should be an unfit witness who ruins the group. אביי has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The killer and the one who sodomizes should save [themselves]! אביי was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a challenge that the 'from behind' answer can't solve. אביי goes silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can picture a victim who didn't see, but the person doing the act always sees it. A person can't testify about himself, so the sinner would always be an unfit witness, and nobody could ever be punished.

keyTerms.meaning: The killer
The one who does the forbidden act
'They should save' themselves
He was silent: he had no answer

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's silence doesn't mean the rule is wrong. The question stays open until רבא answers it in the next step.

phrases.english: The killer and the one who sodomizes should save [themselves]!
phrases.notes: They certainly saw their own act, and a person can't be a witness about himself.

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is אביי, who had no answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Escalates to a case the earlier answer cannot fix
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rule, together with אביי's 'from behind' answers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sinner always sees his own act and can't testify about himself, so he would always ruin the testimony.

steps.title: רבא: only those who establish the matter count
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with the פסוק 'יקום דבר'. The rule is talking only about people who come to establish the matter in court. The killer and the victim are not that kind of witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came before רבא, he said to him: 'Shall a matter be established': the verse is speaking about those who establish the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings the question to רבא, who solves it. He reads the פסוק as limiting the rule to real witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only people who are acting as witnesses can ruin the group. The killer and the victim are the subjects of the case, not people giving testimony, so they don't count at all. This answers all three of רב פפא's challenges together.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A matter shall be established' (דברים 19:15)
Those who establish the matter: the witnesses giving testimony
'The verse is speaking about...'
When he came before [a greater sage]

steps.whatToRemember: Only people who come to testify and establish the matter can ruin a group of witnesses. The killer and the victim are not witnesses at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the next part of the משנה. Only people who act as witnesses ruin the testimony, not people who just happened to see.

phrases.english: When he came before Rava,
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא bringing his question.

phrases.english: he said to him: 'Shall a matter be established'
the verse is speaking about those who establish the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָקוּם דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge אביי could not answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק to define who counts as a witness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone unfit who saw the act, even the sinner or the victim, ruins the testimony
steps.terutzMaskana: Only witnesses who establish the matter in court can ruin the group

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוסי and the two brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה. It quotes רבי יוסי ('in what case is this said') and the line about what two brothers should do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: In what case is this said, etc. What should two brothers do, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next lines of the משנה. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי limits the rule to דיני נפשות. The משנה then says that people who just happened to see, like two brothers in a crowd, don't ruin the testimony. This fits רבא's idea that only real witnesses count.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In what case is this said?': limits a rule
Two brothers who saw the act among a crowd

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
In what case is this said, etc.
What should two brothers do, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only people who act as witnesses ruin the testimony, not people who just happened to see.

steps.title: How does the court question the witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the court says to the witnesses. This would show who came to testify and who just watched.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we speak to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: how does the court question these witnesses? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only real witnesses can ruin the group, the court needs a way to tell who is testifying. The גמרא wants to know the actual words the court uses.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
We say (the court says)
To them (the witnesses)

phrases.english: How do we speak to them?
phrases.notes: 'We' means the judges, and 'them' means the people who saw the act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to put the משנה's rule into practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the court says to the witnesses, to find out who came to testify

steps.title: The court asks: did you come to watch or to testify?
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the court asks the people whether they came to watch or to testify. If they came to testify and one is a relative or unfit, the whole testimony is cancelled. If they came only to watch, they are not counted, just like the two brothers in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what we ask them: 'Did you come to watch, or did you come to testify?' If they say they came to testify, and one of them turns out to be a relative or unfit, their whole testimony is cancelled. If they say they came only to watch, then this is the משנה's case: what should two brothers do who saw someone kill a person?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 15. The court asks each person why he came, and his answer decides whether he is part of the group of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who says he came to testify becomes part of the group, so if he is unfit the whole group falls. A person who says he only came to watch is not part of the group, so he cannot ruin it. This explains the משנה's line about two brothers: brothers who only watched should not ruin the case.

keyTerms.meaning: to watch, to look on
to testify
a relative, who may not be a witness
unfit to be a witness
their testimony is cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about what the person saw. Everyone may have seen the event. What matters is whether he came to court to testify. That is what makes him part of the group of witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical test the court uses. It also fits רבא's idea in step 13: only people who come to establish the matter in court count as witnesses.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what we say to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the people standing before the court, before they testify.

phrases.english: Did you come to watch
or did you come to testify?
If they say they came to testify,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל –
phrases.english: and one of them is found to be a relative or unfit,
their testimony is cancelled.
If they say they came to watch,
what should two brothers do
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's own words, quoted in step 14. Here they show that onlookers should not ruin the case.

phrases.english: who saw someone who killed a person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court asks each person whether he came to watch or to testify. Only those who came to testify count as part of the group.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the final הלכה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules like רבי יוסי. רב נחמן rules like רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי. And רב נחמן says: The הלכה follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports an argument between אמוראים about which opinion in the משנה is the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brought two views, one from רבי יוסי and one from רבי. שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, and רב נחמן rules like רבי. The גמרא is now asking which view we follow in practice, not explaining the views again.

keyTerms.meaning: the final practical ruling follows this opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The court counts as witnesses only people who came to testify. There is an argument about the final הלכה: שמואל follows רבי יוסי, and רב נחמן follows רבי.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.
And Rav Nachman says:
The halacha follows Rabbi.
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' always means רבי יהודה הנשיא, whose view is also in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: איתמר אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל הלכה כרבי יוסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanation of רבי יוסי's view is finished, the גמרא turns to which opinion in the משנה is the final הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is an argument about the final הלכה. שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, and רב נחמן rules like רבי.
